title: The Garden of Ironhollow
premise: Jude Pemberton, a mercenary whose god fell silent three years ago, survives in Ironhollow by selling charms in a city that outlawed magic—until the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, revealing that the country itself was a spell held together by his dead god's last breath. Hunted by the Crown's Wardens and guided by a found family of outcasts—a disgraced cartographer, a child who remembers the stars, and the woman he once swore to kill—Jude must reach the Door at the heart of the old garden where his god died. There he learns he is the god's inheritance: the final ward. In the end, Jude refuses both sacrifice and escape, unmaking the Door and letting the country end honestly, so that what grows in its place can be real.
about_author: Petra Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned estates before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about duty, decay, and the stubborn tenderness of people who refuse to let go.

chapters.title: Charms for a Silent God
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the outlaw city of Vell's Crossing, Jude sells hollow charms and hides the ember of true magic in his chest, haunted by three years of divine silence. A routine sale to a frightened child draws the attention of Warden Sera Ilvane—his former comrade and the woman he betrayed. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety, ending with the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Jude and Sera. The border wards shatter at moonrise and every star above Ironhollow goes dark; the sky shows only a vast, watching absence. Panic floods the city as Wardens begin burning suspected mages. Sera finds Jude mid-escape and, instead of arresting him, demands to know what he knows about the wards' fall. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant alliance between old wounds.

chapters.title: A Cartographer of Vanished Roads
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera brings Jude to Odile Ferrant, a disgraced royal cartographer whose maps redraw themselves nightly as the country literally shrinks—roads dissolving into grey nothing. Odile reveals the truth: Ironhollow was never a place but a spell, and it is being unwound from outside. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your whole world is a dying lie.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Light
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Fleeing Vell's Crossing, the group shelters with smugglers and meets Pip, an orphan born after the Silence who somehow recalls the stars—and hums the god's name without knowing it. Jude realizes Pip carries a fragment of the same divinity sleeping in him. Emotional beat: tenderness kindling; Jude begins choosing people over survival.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera's own order turns on her when she refuses to hand over Pip; she watches the Wardenhall burn its own archives to hide the truth of the god's death. She formally breaks her oaths, an act that should kill her—but doesn't, because the god's law died with the god. Emotional beat: liberation through ruin; love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: The Grey Country
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The party crosses land already unwritten: villages frozen mid-gesture, rivers running upward into blankness. Jude's ember flares each time he protects the others, and each flare accelerates the unraveling—he is burning the country to keep them alive. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve; the cost of care made visible.

chapters.title: An Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the ruined monastery of Saint Verre, Odile deciphers her own family's sealed maps: the Pembertons were the god's gardeners, sworn keepers of the Door, and Jude is the last heir—the living key. Jude rages at a destiny chosen before his birth. Emotional beat: fury at inheritance, and the first acceptance that he cannot walk away.

chapters.title: The Garden Where God Died
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach the iron-walled garden at the country's heart, where the god's corpse has become a tree of black glass—and find the Door already open, held by the entity that silenced the god and is now eating the world beyond. It offers Jude escape: leave, live, forget. Emotional beat: temptation at its sweetest, answered by Pip's small hand in his.

chapters.title: The Last Ward
chapters.summary: Climax, rotating POV across all four. Jude offers himself as the new ward, but Sera and Odile break the choice open: a ward needs willing hands, not one. Pip gives back the starlight she carried, Sera holds the Door's hinge with her broken oath, and Jude unmakes the Door entirely—letting Ironhollow end rather than persist as a cage. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into release.

chapters.title: Seeds in Honest Soil
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Jude's POV. Under a sky slowly relearning its stars, the survivors plant the god's glass-tree seeds in real earth. Jude, no longer a mercenary or a vessel, keeps a small stall again—selling nothing enchanted, only bread. Pip asks if they'll be all right. He says yes, and for the first time means it. Emotional beat: quiet hope; found family rooted where the miracle used to be.
